INPERSON.Menu.Name: Table Mode controls
INPERSON.Menu.Label: Open controls
INPERSON.Menu.Hint: Decide who is sitting at the table and should stop downloading maps.
INPERSON.Settings.Enabled.Name: Enable Table Mode
INPERSON.Settings.Enabled.Hint: Master switch. While this is off, Foundry behaves exactly as usual.
INPERSON.Settings.DefaultPlayers.Name: Include players by default
INPERSON.Settings.DefaultPlayers.Hint: Any player without an explicit assignment in the controls runs in table mode. Gamemasters are never affected unless they opt in themselves.
INPERSON.Settings.Scope.Name: What gets blocked
INPERSON.Settings.Scope.Hint: The default is the background map only - everything else passes. That is the safe choice: a few megabytes too many cost bandwidth, one wrongly blocked file costs the session.
INPERSON.Settings.BlockAudio.Name: Block audio
INPERSON.Settings.BlockAudio.Hint: Stops playlists and ambient sounds from streaming. Short interface sounds (dice, notifications) still play. Note: measured on 2026-08-28, this crashes monks-sound-enhancements whenever a playlist is running - the console then fills with errors once a second.
INPERSON.Settings.AutoNoCanvas.Name: Switch the canvas off entirely in table mode
INPERSON.Settings.AutoNoCanvas.Hint: Also turns on Foundry's "Disable Game Canvas" on affected clients. Saves the WebGL context and render loop on top, but requires the player to reload. Monitor accounts and gamemasters are left alone.
INPERSON.Settings.AllowList.Name: Exceptions
INPERSON.Settings.AllowList.Hint: Path fragments that are never blocked - one per line or comma separated. Example: modules/my-map-assets/
INPERSON.Settings.Self.Name: For this client
INPERSON.Settings.Self.Hint: Applies to this device only. An explicit assignment by the gamemaster always wins.
INPERSON.Panel.Title: Ninjo's In-Person Tools
INPERSON.Panel.MasterHint: Click to stop map downloads on the player clients.
INPERSON.Keybind.OpenPanel.Name: Open Table Mode controls
INPERSON.Keybind.OpenPanel.Hint: Opens the controls without going through the settings. Gamemasters only. Default is Alt+M - Ctrl+T will not work, the browser claims it for a new tab.
INPERSON.Panel.MeasureTooltip: Asks the server for headers only on every file of this scene and reads the file size. That transfers a few hundred bytes even for a 35 MB map. Results are stored, so a scene only needs measuring once.
INPERSON.Panel.CostTooltip: Total of all measured files of this scene, regardless of whether table mode is running. The two lines below split that figure into what gets blocked and what is loaded anyway.
INPERSON.Panel.UnmeasuredTooltip: This many files of the scene have no known size yet. They are missing from the total on the left. Click "Measure" to fill them in.
INPERSON.Panel.MeasureHint: Click "Measure" so this shows real figures instead of an incomplete total.
INPERSON.Panel.MonitorProtected: Protected: this account shows the map on the TV and never enters table mode automatically. Only "Always" overrides that.
INPERSON.Notify.NoScene: No active scene, nothing to measure.
INPERSON.Notify.Measured: Scene measured: {size} per client ({measured} files, {missing} without a size header).
INPERSON.Notify.MeasureFailed: Measuring failed - see the console for details.
INPERSON.Notify.RefreshSent: All connected clients were asked to re-apply their state.
INPERSON.Notify.CanvasDisabled: Table Mode switched the game canvas off on this device.
INPERSON.Notify.CanvasRestored: Table Mode released the game canvas on this device.
INPERSON.Settings.MonitorRelease.Name: When a display is released
INPERSON.Settings.MonitorRelease.Hint: What a display does once its pin is lifted. Without this choice it would sit on the pinned scene until the next activation happens to come along.
INPERSON.Settings.MonitorRelease.Follow: Move to the active scene and follow again
INPERSON.Panel.RolePinnedTip: Stays on its scene until you send it somewhere explicitly.
INPERSON.Notify.NoIdleScene: No idle scene chosen - the display follows the active scene instead.
INPERSON.Notify.DisplayKeptBack: {who} is pinned and was left behind. Use "Bring players here" to take it along on purpose.
INPERSON.Panel.IdleSceneUnused: Currently unused: the module setting "When a display is released" is set to "Move to the active scene".
INPERSON.Settings.MonitorBM.Name: Battlemap display
INPERSON.Settings.MonitorBM.Hint: The account on the map screen. It follows every scene activation as usual and is only exempt from table mode, so it actually shows the map.
INPERSON.Settings.MonitorSC.Name: Scene display
INPERSON.Settings.MonitorSC.Hint: The account that can be pinned. While pinned it stays on its scene no matter what you activate - except when the activated battlemap names a companion scene, in which case it moves there.
INPERSON.Notify.NoSceneDisplay: No scene display chosen. Pick an account under "Scene display" in the module settings.
INPERSON.SceneConfig.Companion: Companion scene for the scene display
INPERSON.SceneConfig.CompanionHint: When this scene is activated the scene display switches to the chosen companion - even while pinned. Meant for battlemaps that have a matching scene view.
INPERSON.SceneConfig.RotationHint: Rotates the whole view of this scene, for everyone who sees it. Meant for maps drawn portrait that should lie across the width of a 16:9 screen. Note: the token HUD turns with it and will sit sideways too.
INPERSON.SceneConfig.LockViewCorrected: Lock View detected: its "{mode}" fitting and the viewbox are turned along with this scene.
INPERSON.SceneConfig.LockViewViewboxOnly: Lock View detected: the viewbox is turned along with this scene. The fitting needs no correction.
INPERSON.SceneConfig.LockViewOffset: Lock View detected, but this scene excludes the sidebar or the AV dock from the view. Those offsets are measured on screen and are not turned along, so the viewbox stays slightly off while the scene is rotated.
INPERSON.Pull.Title: Bring players
INPERSON.Pull.NobodyOnline: Nobody except you is connected right now.
INPERSON.Notify.Migrated: Carried over from the previous version: {settings} settings, {scenes} scenes.
INPERSON.Notify.DefaultCompanionSet: "{scene}" is now the default companion scene.
INPERSON.Panel.DefaultCompanionTip: Where the scene display goes when a battlemap is activated that names no companion of its own. Without it an unpinned display shows the same map as the battlemap display - the one thing a second screen need not do. A companion named on the battlemap itself always wins.
INPERSON.Settings.IdleAfter.Name: Screensaver after ... minutes of quiet
INPERSON.Settings.IdleAfter.Hint: How long nothing may happen before the scene display starts protecting itself. 0 switches the screensaver off. Quiet means nobody but the displays themselves is doing anything - cursors, scene changes, rulers and rolls all reset the clock.
INPERSON.Settings.IdleFolder.Name: Screensaver folder
INPERSON.Settings.IdleFolder.Hint: The scenes in this folder are shown one after another. With only one in it the display simply goes there and stays - handy for a picture that has movement of its own. Leave it empty to skip straight to the black screen.
INPERSON.Settings.IdleRotate.Name: Change scene every ... minutes
INPERSON.Settings.IdleRotate.Hint: Gap between two scenes of the folder while it stays quiet.
INPERSON.Displays.MenuHint: Accounts, companion scenes and burn-in protection - everything about the two screens on a page of its own.
INPERSON.Displays.Title: Set up scene displays
INPERSON.Displays.AccountsHint: Which account drives which screen. The names can be anything; both are automatically exempt from table mode.
INPERSON.Displays.BurnInHint: For displays on an OLED. After a while without activity the display cycles through a folder and lays a black cover over the picture in between. The cover lifts again when its time is up - the aim is not to switch the television off, only that no picture stands still for hours.
INPERSON.Settings.IdleBlankFor.Name: Cover stays for ... minutes
INPERSON.Settings.IdleBlankFor.Hint: Then it lifts and the scene is visible again until the waiting time above has passed once more. Black and picture take turns rather than the screen staying dark for good.
INPERSON.Settings.IdleLogo.Name: Image on the cover
INPERSON.Settings.IdleLogo.Hint: Drifts slowly across the black. Without one a small gold dot appears instead, so the screen does not look broken.
INPERSON.Displays.PairsHint: Battlemaps with a companion of their own. They can be made and undone here; the same pairing also appears in that battlemap's own scene configuration.
INPERSON.Settings.KeepTokens.Name: Keep loading token artwork
INPERSON.Settings.KeepTokens.Hint: Recommended. Token images are small and players need to tell their figures apart. Turning this off leaves tokens black as well.
INPERSON.Settings.HideProgress.Name: Hide the loading bar for players
INPERSON.Settings.HideProgress.Hint: Foundry shows its scene loading bar even when every file comes from the browser cache or was blocked. It reports processing, not bandwidth, which is misleading here. This only hides the display, nothing about loading changes.
INPERSON.Settings.ShowPill.Name: Show status indicator
INPERSON.Settings.ShowPill.Hint: Small badge along the bottom edge of a player's screen while table mode runs there. It explains that the black map is deliberate.
INPERSON.Settings.IdleEnabled.Name: Use a screensaver
INPERSON.Settings.IdleEnabled.Hint: For displays on an OLED. With this off nothing happens at all - everything below appears only once you say yes here.
INPERSON.Settings.IdleMode.Name: Which kind
INPERSON.Settings.IdleMode.Hint: The cover is much the stronger of the two: on an OLED a black pixel is off and does not age at all, while another bright scene wears the panel exactly as the first one did. The scene swap is for tables that would rather look at something.
INPERSON.Settings.IdleMode.Cover: Lay a black cover over the current scene
INPERSON.Displays.TestCoverHint: Shows it here for a few seconds - a click or a key dismisses it. The mark is sized against the screen, so it looks the same on this monitor as it will on the television.
INPERSON.TableMode.MenuHint: What the devices at the table stop loading, and who it applies to.
INPERSON.TableMode.Title: Set up table mode
INPERSON.TableMode.StateOff: Table mode is off. It is switched on and off in the controls, where you can also see who it affects.
INPERSON.SceneField.Empty: None — drag a scene here from the sidebar to set one
INPERSON.SceneField.NotAScene: That was not a scene. Only entries from the scene sidebar can be dropped here.
INPERSON.SceneField.NotItself: A scene cannot be its own companion.
INPERSON.Displays.PairNeedsBoth: Choose both sides: the battlemap first, then the scene the display should show alongside it.
INPERSON.Displays.PairMade: "{scene}" now shows "{companion}" on the scene display.
INPERSON.Settings.ActorPanel.Name: Replace Sheet Only's actor selector
INPERSON.Settings.ActorPanel.Hint: In sheet-only mode, replaces the selector button with an actor directory that docks to the right edge; the character sheet makes room for it. Requires the "Sheet Only" module and has no effect without it.
INPERSON.Settings.ClockStrip.Name: Date and time in sheet-only mode
INPERSON.Settings.ClockStrip.Hint: Shows a slim strip with the date and time while only the character sheet is visible. There is no Foundry interface left in that mode, and so no calendar HUD either. Applies to this device only.
INPERSON.Settings.ClockWeather.Name: Include weather and season
INPERSON.Settings.ClockWeather.Hint: Adds the season to the strip and, where there is one, the current weather with its temperature. The season is read from the world calendar and needs nothing else - Foundry's own calendar is enough. The weather comes from Calendaria; without it that part is simply left out.
INPERSON.Trade.Broken: The trade did not go through completely. What was meant and what happened is written in the "Tauschbuch" journal.
INPERSON.Settings.Trade.Name: Trading between players
INPERSON.Settings.Trade.Hint: Adds a trade button. Two players put items and money on a table; nothing moves until both agree. Built for fingers and works in Sheet Only mode.
INPERSON.Settings.TradeWithGM.Name: Allow trading with the gamemaster
INPERSON.Settings.TradeWithGM.Hint: Otherwise the partner list shows fellow players only. A gamemaster hands things out directly anyway; a request they have to answer is a detour for them.
INPERSON.Settings.TradeLog.Name: Record trades in the logbook
INPERSON.Settings.TradeLog.Hint: Writes an entry into the "Tauschbuch" journal before each trade and adds what actually happened afterwards. Visible to gamemasters only. If the moving goes wrong, that entry says what was meant.
INPERSON.Trade.Title: Trade
INPERSON.Trade.AskHint: {who} is offering the trade. Only players who are logged in right now are listed.
INPERSON.Trade.NobodyOnline: There is nobody here to trade with at the moment.
INPERSON.Trade.NoGM: A trade needs a gamemaster logged in - only they may create and remove items on somebody else's character.
INPERSON.Trade.NoCharacter: You have no character assigned. A gamemaster can set that in your user account.
INPERSON.Trade.AsksYou: {who} would like to trade with you.
INPERSON.Trade.NoItems: This character carries nothing that could be handed over.
INPERSON.Trade.Busy: One of you is already in a trade.
INPERSON.Trade.Why.none: no character - a gamemaster can assign one in the account settings
INPERSON.Trade.Why.many: owns several characters - one has to be assigned in the account settings
INPERSON.Trade.NobodyReady: Somebody is here, but nobody has a character assigned. A gamemaster sets that in the user account under "Character".
INPERSON.Trade.PickOne: You own several characters but none is assigned to you. Until then it is not clear who is trading.
INPERSON.Trade.Over.Broken: The trade with {who} was not carried out in full. Speak to the gamemaster - the logbook says what was meant.
INPERSON.Trade.Over.ICancelled: You called off the trade with {who}.
INPERSON.Clock.MenuHint: What the strip above the character sheet shows - date, time, weather, season - each switched on and off on its own. Applies to every player.
INPERSON.Clock.Title: Time & weather
INPERSON.Clock.Field.StripHint: The master switch. Off means no strip, whatever is ticked below.
INPERSON.Clock.Field.SeasonHint: Comes from the world calendar and needs no calendar module.
INPERSON.Clock.NoWeatherSource: No weather module active - has no effect for now.
INPERSON.Clock.Group.Strip: The strip above the character sheet
INPERSON.Clock.Group.StripHint: Applies to the whole table. What is set here is what every player in Sheet Only sees.
INPERSON.TradeSettings.MenuHint: Whether players may trade with one another, whether the gamemaster appears as a partner, and whether every trade is recorded in the logbook.
INPERSON.TradeSettings.Title: Trading
INPERSON.TradeSettings.GroupHint: Two people put items and money on a table; nothing moves until both agree. It is always carried out on the gamemaster's client - with no gamemaster logged in there is no trade.
INPERSON.TradeSettings.ItemPiles: Item Piles is active. Turn its trade button off, or two will sit side by side.
INPERSON.Willkommen.Einleitung: Tools for groups playing around one table. Player tablets stop downloading battlemaps, two displays can be steered separately, and portrait maps lie down flat.
INPERSON.Willkommen.Punkt1: Table mode — keeps map downloads off the players' devices. Measured: one "preload scene" transferred 58.86 MB, and 0.00 MB with table mode on.
INPERSON.Willkommen.Punkt2: Scene displays — two display accounts with separate jobs: one follows every scene, one can be pinned. Plus burn-in protection for the television.
INPERSON.Willkommen.Punkt3: On the character sheet — together with Sheet Only, the date, time and weather appear where there is otherwise no interface left.
INPERSON.Willkommen.Start: To begin: Alt+T opens the control panel with the master switch. Everything else lives in the module settings under "Table Mode" and "Scene Displays".
INPERSON.Willkommen.Untertitel: Tools for playing around a real table
INPERSON.Willkommen.ForgeZeile: Every module, its documentation and the German translations in one place — open the module page
INPERSON.Clock.Field.SkyHint: Shows where the sun or moon stands right now, with the moon's phase. Computed from the world calendar; without those figures it falls back to 06:00/18:00.
INPERSON.Clock.SunGuessed: estimated - the calendar gives no figures
INPERSON.SheetView.Name: Sheet view (beta)
INPERSON.SheetView.Hint: Gives players the whole screen for their character sheet and replaces Foundry's interface with a bar of a few large buttons. For tablets at the table. Beta: switch it on while you are there - gamemasters are never affected.
INPERSON.SheetView.NoFullscreen: This device does not allow fullscreen. On iPhone and iPad, use “Add to Home Screen”.
INPERSON.SheetView.MenuHint: Which accounts see only their character sheet, whether their canvas is switched off, and how the bar behaves. Gamemasters are never affected.
INPERSON.SheetView.Title: Sheet view (beta)
INPERSON.SheetView.GroupHint: Foundry's interface disappears, the sheet fills the screen, and a small bar keeps characters, chat, journal and trading at hand. For tablets at the table. Beta: switch it on while you are there.
INPERSON.SheetView.EnabledHint: The master switch. Off means nobody gets the view, whoever is ticked below.
INPERSON.SheetView.WhoListHint: Ticked accounts only. A player on a laptop needs the scene list - one on a tablet does not. Accounts without an assigned character stay in the normal interface even when ticked.
INPERSON.SheetView.NoUsers: There are no player accounts yet.
INPERSON.SheetView.NoCanvasHint: The tablet stops rendering scenes altogether - the same machinery as table mode. The device asks once to reload.
INPERSON.SheetView.ChatOnUse: Open the chat on a roll
INPERSON.SheetView.ChatOnUseHint: As soon as the player rolls or uses something themselves, the chat opens so they see the result. Other people's rolls open nothing.
INPERSON.SheetView.ResetHint: Reset this account's bars to their defaults - position, size, text size, on all of its devices. A device that is off catches up on its next load.
INPERSON.SheetView.ResetDone: {name}: bars are being reset to their defaults.
